quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Where can a motorcycle operator use a complete traffic lane?

options.text: On all highways and streets where motorcycles are allowed
Nowhere. Motorcyclists must share lanes with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all highways and streets where motorcycles are allowed
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists have the right to use a complete traffic lane on any road where motorcycles are legal. Two motorcyclists or moped riders can ride next to each other in one lane if they choose.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars behind you.
Move when the vehicle ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look to your left first. Traffic from the left is closer to you than traffic from the right. Then look right. Finally, look left again in case you missed any vehicles the first time.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the driver can see you.
Honk your horn to alert the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Never drive in someone else's blind spot. Move ahead or fall back so the other driver can see you clearly.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, yield to any pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles still in the intersection. You can proceed, but drive at a speed where you can stop if the light changes before you reach the intersection.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or sleet makes the road slippery. Poor road conditions may require you to drive slower than the posted speed limit for safety.

questions.question: Drivers should watch carefully for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many accidents happen because drivers are looking but still don't see motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians. These are smaller, move faster, and have less noticeable lights than larger vehicles. Always stay alert for them.

questions.question: While waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn, you should:

options.text: Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to get drivers to let you through.
Drive around the rear of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels prevent you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light has the same meaning as:
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red light, you must stop and let all other traffic pass before going.

questions.question: You must use your headlights when people or vehicles cannot be clearly seen 1,000 feet away.
questions.explanation: Use headlights from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise. Also use them anytime people or vehicles cannot be clearly seen 1,000 feet away.

questions.question: You must always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers what you are doing and help prevent accidents.

questions.question: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to light up the road.

questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, slow down and drive carefully. Do not use high beam headlights. Low beams work better in fog to light up the road and objects ahead.

questions.question: When driving in rain, you must:
questions.explanation: In rain, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, which one has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car coming from the right.
The car coming from the left.
The car whose driver honks first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, you must yield to a vehicle coming from your right.

questions.question: At night, you may use parking lights instead of headlights.
questions.explanation: You cannot drive at night using only parking lights. You must use your headlights when it is dark or visibility is poor.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see it.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down. Do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren nearby but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot whenever you change your vehicle's position. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, complete the turn into:

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to the direction you came from. Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Other vehicles can follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two people is more balanced than one with one rider.
You must move completely into the left lane when passing a motorcycle.
A motorcycle's brake lights always turn on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must move completely into the left lane when passing a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full lane. Make sure your vehicle is completely in the left lane before passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare you for upcoming road conditions. This yellow sign with black markings warns you that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let traffic merge safely.

questions.question: You should leave extra space when stopping:
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, you will have room to avoid a collision.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you are driving. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on your hazard lights and hold tight.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: If your power steering fails, you will need to push harder to steer. Slow down your vehicle and carefully drive to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: What affects braking distance?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road surface.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on three things: how fast you are driving, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road surface.

questions.question: Defensive driving means:

options.text: Using safe driving methods to avoid crashes.
It is more dangerous than regular driving.
It is not a good idea.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving methods to avoid crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe driving methods to avoid crashes. You adjust your driving based on weather, how you feel, and what other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians are doing.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main road space.
Tell the other vehicle to pull over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main road space.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give vehicles coming toward you at least half of the main road space. Both vehicles need enough room to pass each other safely.

questions.question: Compared to daytime driving, night driving is:
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than daytime driving. It is harder to see, bright lights from other cars can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: At dusk or on cloudy days, you should:

options.text: Drive with your four-way flashers on.
Drive with your parking lights on.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on cloudy days. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle and within 500 feet of a vehicle you are following. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give directions.

questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles (police cars, fire trucks, ambulances) pass when they use sirens or horns and have red or blue flashing lights. Follow any directions they give over loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only go when you know it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is coming toward you. Your headlights should be:

options.text: On either bright or low beam.

questions.explanation: Do not use bright headlights when an oncoming vehicle is near or when you are following another vehicle at night. Switch to low beam to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road turns sharply right, then left.
The road turns sharply left, then right.
The road curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a roundabout is ahead. Slow down and enter the roundabout at a low speed. Let traffic already in the roundabout go first.

questions.question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is true?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive poorly enough to look drunk.
Opening a window and turning up the radio keeps them alert.
Only older drivers get drowsy while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive poorly enough to look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so badly that they look drunk. Opening a window, turning on the radio, or drinking coffee does not make a drowsy driver alert to road hazards.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After turning, your car should be in:

options.text: The lane with the least traffic.

questions.explanation: When turning left onto a one-way street, end your turn in the lane closest to the lane you just left.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Less if you drink beer instead of wine.
Less if you drink wine instead of beer.
Most if you drink hard ciders and mixed drinks.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: All types of alcohol hurt your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines in the center of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
A road with rules about stereo volume.
A TV show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, in the rear, and in front. Cars cannot be seen in these areas. These blind spots are called the "No zone."

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign tell you?

options.text: It warns of hazards ahead or possible hazards.
Food and gas locations are ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns of hazards ahead or possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about driving hazards. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: When turning, you must ____ your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning. Lower your speed to keep control of your car, stay in your lane, and be ready for unexpected situations.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side of the street.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They get you ready for road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns you that cyclists may cross the road.

questions.question: When an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Watch what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic lights help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey traffic signals. The only exception is when a police officer is directing traffic.

questions.question: Which substance may impair your driving and result in a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and some legal medicines like prescription and over-the-counter drugs.

questions.question: This is a ____ sign.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign is a Yield sign. Slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and other vehicles pass first. Only stop if needed.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift to neutral and press the brake steadily. When safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Turn the wheel in the direction of the skid.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm. Turn the steering wheel in the direction the vehicle is skidding.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow and black. They prepare you for road hazards. This sign tells you a lane is ending. Prepare to merge safely with other traffic.

questions.question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Hide that you don't know the vehicle.
Ignore any problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take time to learn where everything is and how it works before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take time to learn where everything is and how it works before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, learn the locations of the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back.
Keep driving and take the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving and take the next exit.
questions.explanation: Don't make a sudden turn at the last moment to catch your exit. If you miss it, go to the next exit.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Always use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and can blind you.

questions.question: What colors are used for warning signs about upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on white background
Black letters or symbols on yellow background
White letters or symbols on blue background
White letters or symbols on green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. Work zone warning signs are orange with black letters or symbols.
